Specifically, deciding whether "generic" vs. "personalized" outreach justifies contacting more students (Q7) dictates how aggressively we should tune the algorithm's selectivity versus accuracy in Q3. If our intervention strategy isn't tailored right, even perfect data usage fails to help the student.

Reflecting on my survey responses as S4: Q6 was clear but challenged me to weigh "early help" against "intrusion." Q4 is arguably most critical: without clear reasons for intervention, trust collapses. However, Q6 and Q7 are equally vital in practice. For me, the trade-off between accuracy and transparency is crucial; I cannot accept being flagged by an opaque system, even if it helps more people overall.
